subject: OPEN statement (validation of fixed file attributes)
notes: The A.1 item 129 determination is made and documented, and was RE-DECIDED on 2026-09-07 (kb/Work PB802, owner decision verbatim: 'Let's match GNUCobol's implementation in spirit. No sidecar of any type.'). THE DETERMINATION IS NOW ONE RULE: the validated set is exactly what each organization's PHYSICAL FORMAT ENCODES, using the latitude GR10 grants in its own words ('The implementor defines which of the fixed-file attributes are validated during the execution of the OPEN statement. The validation of fixed-file attributes may vary depending on the organization or storage medium of the file.'). Fixed-length record sequential and line sequential record nothing and validate nothing (9.1.7.2; 9.1.13.2 items 3, 5 and 7 answer the disagreements with the successful '04', '06' and '09'). A RECORD VARYING record-sequential file records its record type in 9.1.7.2's record-length header, so that header must PARSE - and only that: a prefix outside the RECORD clause's bounds is item 3's '04', not a '39'. RELATIVE and INDEXED record the organization, record type, the two logical record sizes and the key table in the framed store's header, IN the data file; an unreadable header is '39' and a zero-byte file is the one tolerated exception. THE KEY CHECK HAS A DOCUMENTED RUNTIME OPT-OUT, WISEOWL_COBOL_KEYCHECK=OFF - GnuCOBOL's COB_KEYCHECK under this repository's naming (WISEOWL_COBOL_, never COBOL_, which is the external-switch family's prefix), read once per run unit in FileRegistry and registered in RuntimeConfig; it narrows the set by exactly the key table and is part of the determination rather than an escape from it. The set is still NOT the empty set item 50 answers for DELETE FILE. The code set is still outside the set, on PB793's ground (13.18.13.4 GR7 vs GR2/GR6 really can differ now, so it is a determination and not an observation that the value is constant): a CODE-SET clause exists to read a file some OTHER system wrote, which carries no WiseOwl COBOL header, and reading a converted file through a description with no CODE-SET clause is GR7's own default. The physical record sizes (no blocking; BLOCK CONTAINS inert under A.3 item 5) and the record delimiter (no compiler surface; the realized distinction is a sequential-organization attribute whose format records nothing) are outside it too. 9.1.6's last sentence is still answered NO - shareability is per file connector (14.9.27.4 GR21-GR23), arbitrated live (9.1.15 Table 19). TWO OWNER-VISIBLE CONSEQUENCES ARE DOCUMENTED RATHER THAN SILENT: the store header is a FORMAT CHANGE (a relative or indexed file from an earlier build is refused '39' instead of silently misread), and a keyed store reopened through a SEQUENTIAL description now opens '00' where the catalog answered '39'. || editions 85,2002,2014,2023 (kb/Work PB3173, S0b; DESIGN-conformance-suite.md §6 step 0): a facility that exists at every edition (the COBOL-85 nucleus, I-O, inter-program and SPECIAL-NAMES implementor-names; its arithmetic, the only arithmetic of COBOL-85, is what later editions name native).
